chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: He narrated to me Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) that he said:
O Ali! Four characteristics are among the signs of misery: solidity of the eye, hard-heartedness, having high aspirations, and the love for a very long life.

key_terms.بُعْدُ الْأَمَلِ: having high aspirations, often implying excessive hope in worldly life
key_terms.جَمُودُ الْعَيْنِ: solidity/fixedness of the eye, implying lack of insight or reflection
key_terms.حُبُّ الْبَقَاءِ: love for a very long life, attachment to worldly duration

ai.seo_question: What are the four signs of misery according to the Prophet in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) identifies four spiritual pathologies that lead to human wretchedness, linking physical demeanor with inner states. 'Jamud al-ayn' (a fixed or unreflective gaze) signifies a lack of contemplation, while 'qasawat al-qalb' (hardness of heart) blocks divine mercy. The combination of 'ba'd al-amal' (distant hope, often interpreted as complacency in delaying repentance) and 'hub al-baqa' (love of longevity/worldliness) illustrates how attachment to the temporal self prevents spiritual elevation.
